criteria.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core using a fake gh Runner that returns a red run for the SHA and a failing shard job log containing a cargo 'failures:' list shows the failed CheckRun (via run_routed_with_record) has passed=false, failed_tests equal to the listed names, and a non-empty output_tail holding the last lines of the log. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: gh::tests::red_reused_run_records_failing_tests_and_log_tail passed. It calls crate::routing::run_routed_with_record with GhClient::new(&runner,..).ci_source(CI_BRANCH) and the CiRunner fake. That fake serves a red run, a failed `test (shard 1)` job with id 77, and a stamped log for actions/jobs/77/logs. The test asserts !passed && reused, failed_tests == ["athena_core tests::a", "athena_core tests::b"], an output_tail that starts with the failing-units line and ends with the last log line, no timestamps, that nothing ran locally, and that the logs path was requested. The full suite passed in the recorded CI run (`cargo test --locked`).

criteria.criterion: A test builds the verifier input/brief from that failed check record and asserts the brief text contains the failing test names and the log tail, and the instruction to run only the failing tests with cargo test -p <crate> <name> unless there is a reason to run more. Run: cargo test -p athena-context -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: run::tests::...::ci_reuse_red_test_shard_hands_the_verifier_the_failing_tests_and_log_tail passed. The briefs.rs tests verifier_brief_shows_failing_tests_and_log_tail_and_tells_it_to_run_only_those, verifier_brief_without_failing_test_data_is_as_it_was and verifier_brief_clips_a_long_tail... passed. verify::tests::check_result_view_shows_names_units_and_tail_only_for_a_reused_failed_check passed.

findings.summary: The `failing units:` header is lost whenever the CI log has 200 or more lines, which is normal for a real test shard.
findings.evidence: Found by reading the code, not by running it. detail_from_job_logs trims the joined log to tail_lines(text, FAILED_TAIL_LINES=200), then prepends `failing units: ...\n`, which makes 201 lines. with_failure_detail then applies tail_lines(&output_tail, FAILED_TAIL_LINES) again, and that drops the first line, the header. Every test uses a short log, so none catches this. Effect: for real logs, check_result_view finds no header, the brief has no 'Failing units' line, and the run-only text still mentions 'The failing-units line'. The CHANGELOG's 'led by a failing units line' is also wrong for long logs. The names, the tail and the instruction still reach the verifier. Fix: cap the log at FAILED_TAIL_LINES-1 lines before adding the header, or add the header after the final cap in with_failure_detail.

summary: The change does what was asked. When Athena reuses a red GitHub run, `CiBranchSource::failure_detail` reads the log of each failed `test (shard N)` job through the existing gh client, the same `actions/jobs/<id>/logs` call the client already makes elsewhere. It records the cargo `failures:` names (`<binary> <test>`) and a redacted, capped log tail on the failed `test` CheckRun. The verifier brief then lists those names and the quoted tail, and tells the verifier to run only those tests with `cargo test -p <crate> <name>` unless it has a reason to run more. If the log can't be read, has no `failures:` list, or redaction fails, the check is recorded as a plain failure, as it is today. A green run makes no log call. Partial lists carry markers in parentheses, so they are never judged pre-existing against the base. I ran every planned demonstration test and all passed: criterion 1 (gh fake runner through `run_routed_with_record`), criterion 2 (an end-to-end `Athena::go` run showing the verifier prompt, plus briefs.rs unit tests), criterion 3 (the fallback and green-run tests), and criterion 7 (the existing verify and local output-tail tests). Grep confirms what the CHANGELOG audit says about each other reader. I found two minor problems. First, run/verification.rs changed but is not on the deliverables list; it is a small, planned change that wires the new view into the verifier input. Second, the `failing units:` header line is dropped from the recorded tail whenever the CI log has 200 or more lines, which real shard logs do (I found this by reading the code, not by running it). The test names, the tail and the run-only instruction are not affected.
